ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: The figure is an ideal op-amp circuit, and the op-amp is marked with supply/saturation values +15 V and -12 V. One end of capacitor C is grounded, and the other end is connected to the inverting input terminal of the op-amp; the voltage of this node is labeled Vc. The op-amp output is fed back through a resistor R to this inverting input node. The non-inverting input terminal of the op-amp is connected to the network below composed of several equal resistors R and ideal diodes D; one end of this network is grounded, and the other end is driven by the op-amp output. On the right side, the I_D-V_D characteristic of the ideal diode is also drawn. Then reason: The ideal op-amp output switches only between the two saturation values +15 V and -12 V. The diode-resistor network at the non-inverting terminal provides reference thresholds that change with the output polarity. When Vo = +15 V, the corresponding diode conducts and bypasses one equal resistor, making the reference voltage at the non-inverting terminal one third of the output, namely V+ = 15/3 = +5 V. The capacitor voltage Vc at the inverting terminal changes through the feedback resistor until Vc reaches +5 V, when the output flips, so the maximum value of Vc is +5 V. When Vo = -12 V, the diode in the opposite direction conducts and bypasses the resistor on the other side, making the reference voltage at the non-inverting terminal two thirds of the output, namely V+ = 2(-12)/3 = -8 V. When the capacitor voltage changes to -8 V, the output flips again, so the minimum value of Vc is -8 V. Therefore the difference between the maximum and minimum values of the capacitor voltage is 5 - (-8) = 13 V.

raw_record.question_text: For the following circuit with an ideal OPAMP, the difference between the maximum and minimum values of the capacitor voltage \(V_c\) is ______ V.

method.method_draft: First describe the image: an ideal op-amp has a capacitor voltage Vc at the inverting input, an R feedback path from output to that node, and a diode-resistor network feeding the non-inverting input from the output and ground. Treat the op-amp output as saturated at +15 V or -12 V. For Vo = +15 V, determine which ideal diode conducts in the lower divider; the conducting diode bypasses one of the equal resistors so the non-inverting reference becomes one-third of the output, V+ = +15/3 = +5 V. The capacitor at the inverting input charges through the feedback resistor until Vc reaches this threshold, at which point the output switches. For Vo = -12 V, the opposite diode conducts and bypasses the opposite resistor, making the non-inverting reference two-thirds of the output, V+ = 2(-12)/3 = -8 V. The capacitor then moves until Vc reaches -8 V and the output switches back. Therefore the maximum and minimum capacitor voltages are +5 V and -8 V, so their difference is 5 - (-8) = 13 V.
method.CoT_raw: 先描述图像：图中是一个理想运放电路，运放标有供电/饱和值 +15 V 和 -12 V。电容 C 一端接地，另一端接到运放反相输入端，该节点电压标为 Vc；运放输出通过一个电阻 R 反馈到该反相输入节点。运放同相输入端接到下方由若干相等电阻 R 和理想二极管 D 组成的网络，该网络一端接地，另一端由运放输出驱动。右侧还画出了理想二极管的 I_D-V_D 特性。再推理：理想运放输出只在 +15 V 和 -12 V 两个饱和值之间切换。同相端的二极管-电阻网络提供随输出极性改变的参考阈值。当 Vo = +15 V 时，对应二极管导通并旁路一个相等电阻，使同相端参考电压为输出的三分之一，即 V+ = 15/3 = +5 V。反相端电容电压 Vc 经反馈电阻变化，直到 Vc 达到 +5 V 时输出翻转，所以 Vc 的最大值为 +5 V。当 Vo = -12 V 时，相反方向的二极管导通并旁路另一侧电阻，使同相端参考电压为输出的三分之二，即 V+ = 2(-12)/3 = -8 V。电容电压变化到 -8 V 时输出再翻转，所以 Vc 的最小值为 -8 V。因此电容电压最大值与最小值之差为 5 - (-8) = 13 V。
